title: No-Code Builder Lab: Apps & Automation
blurb: Two career-changing skills in one lab: turn a web project into a real Android APK using only your browser (from the Team21 MaDSkillz manual), and build your first business automation with Make or Zapier — no code, no command line, ever.

modules.t: Zero to Android APK I: GitHub & Your Project
modules.d: Account, hidden files, and your first repository — every click matters.
modules.body:
What you are about to do

Take a downloaded project file and turn it into a real Android app you can install on any phone — without touching a command line. First time through: ~45 minutes. Every time after: ~10.

Set up GitHub (5 min)

  • Sign up at github.com — real email, strong password, and a professional username (it becomes part of your public URL forever).
  • Verify the email code (check spam for noreply@github.com) and skip the personalization questions.

Prepare your files (3 min)

  • Extract the project zip (right-click → Extract All on Windows; double-click on Mac).
  • Critical: show hidden files. The project contains a .github folder — invisible by default — holding the instructions GitHub uses to build your APK. Windows: View → Show → Hidden items. Mac: Command + Shift + . (period).
Critical checkpoint: confirm you can SEE the .github folder before continuing. If you cannot see it, you cannot upload it — and your APK will never build.

Create the repository (5 min)

  • GitHub → + icon → New repository → name it in lowercase-with-dashes → set Public (required for free builds and public links).
  • Leave README / .gitignore / license unchecked — your zip already contains them; checking them creates conflicts.

quiz.q: Why must you make hidden files visible before uploading?
opts: The .github folder contains the APK build instructions
GitHub requires it for all accounts

modules.t: Zero to Android APK II: Upload, Build & Install
modules.d: Watch GitHub build your app automatically — then put it on a phone.
modules.body:
Upload (10 min)

  • On your empty repo page click "uploading an existing file." Arrange your folder window and browser side by side.
  • Select everything inside the project folder (Ctrl/Cmd + A — confirm .github is highlighted) and drag it into the upload area.
  • If GitHub warns "This file is hidden" — continue; it is supposed to be.
  • Commit with a short message like "Initial upload." Verify src, public, .github, and package.json all appear.

Watch the magic (Actions tab)

The moment .github lands, GitHub starts building your Android APK on its own servers. Open Actions → click the "Build Android APK" run → watch each step turn green: checkout, Node.js, Java JDK, Android SDK, dependencies, web build, Capacitor sync, APK build, artifact upload.

First build: 5–10 minutes (GitHub downloads the whole Android toolkit). Future builds: ~2 minutes. A red ❌ is fixable — see the troubleshooting module.

Download & install (5 min)

  • Bottom of the successful run → Artifacts → click the artifact name → unzip → your .apk file.
  • Get it to your phone (email, Drive, messaging, or USB) → tap it → allow "Install from this source" (normal for non-Play-Store apps) → Install → Open.
You just built and installed a real Android app without writing a line of code or installing any developer tools. That is a genuine builder credential.

quiz.q: Where do you download the freshly built APK?
opts: The Artifacts section of the successful Actions run

modules.t: Zero to Android APK III: Releases, Updates & Troubleshooting
modules.d: Public download links, version discipline, and calm fixes.
modules.body:
Create a public download link (Releases)

  • Repo page → Releases → Create a new release → tag v1.0.0 → title and description ("First public release. Android 8.0+").
  • Publish. The tag triggers a fresh build; ~5 minutes later your APK appears under Assets on a page anyone can access — no login. Share it anywhere, or print a QR code.

Making changes forever after

  • Navigate to any file → pencil icon → edit in the browser like a document (your contact info, program names, colors) → commit → a new APK builds automatically.
  • Version discipline: v1.0.0 → v1.0.1 small fixes · → v1.1.0 new features · → v2.0.0 major redesign.

Troubleshooting the calm way

  • Red ❌ / "TypeScript" error: replace capacitor.config.ts with capacitor.config.json.
  • "Lock file not found": edit the workflow file — remove the "cache: npm" line and change "npm ci" to "npm install."
  • "No such file: dist": the web build failed earlier — check the log; usually a typo in your last edit; revert via file history.
  • Empty Artifacts: build not finished, or it failed — check for the ❌.
  • "Allow from this source" missing: varies by phone brand — check Settings → Apps → Special app access → Install unknown apps.
  • APK crashes on open: phone likely below Android 8.0.
When you finish: test every feature, share the release link with 3 people, watch where they get confused, ship v1.0.1 with one improvement. Repeat — that is how every great app evolves.

modules.t: Your First Business Automation: Form → Instant Email
modules.d: Make.com and Zapier, step by step — the workflow that powers thousands of businesses.
modules.body:
What we are building

Someone fills out your Google Form → the automation sees it → they instantly receive a thank-you email. No manual work. (Real example: a yoga instructor's class registration auto-sends details, location, and time.)

Step 1 — the form

Create a Google Form with at least a Name and an Email field — the email field is how the automation knows who to reply to.

Option A — Make.com

  • Create a scenario → app: Google Forms → Watch Responses → connect your Google account → select your form.
  • Add action: Gmail → Send an Email → in "To," click the field selector (dots icon) and choose the form's email field → write subject and message → you can insert their Name the same way.
  • Save → Test (submit the form yourself) → toggle ON.

Option B — Zapier

  • Create a Zap → Trigger: Google Forms → New Response in Form → choose the form → test the trigger.
  • Action: Gmail → Send Email → map the To/Subject/Body fields, inserting form answers where you want them → test → name the Zap → publish ON.

Which tool?

  • New to automation → Zapier (simplest interface, 6000+ integrations).
  • Planning many automations → Make (stronger free plan, very fast).

Troubleshooting

  • No email sent → check Gmail connection status, confirm the form has an email field, check spam.
  • Name/email missing in the reply → you typed text instead of selecting the form field — go back and use the field selector.
Next steps: add the response to Google Sheets, notify yourself by SMS or chat, auto-create calendar events. You now understand the core concept behind thousands of business automations — the same one you will scale in AI Unlocked Level 2: OPERATE.
